newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices edge higher on cooling demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices edge higher on cooling demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices continued to climb Wednesday as the heat in the Southwest kept buyers's clutch on the market and forecasts called for warmer weather in the Northeast and Midwest, industry sources said.

"It's heat perception. It was up early but then fell off again late. There's also talk of a tropical depression off the coast of Africa. They're just looking for something to drive this market higher," one Houston-based trader said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast gas at the Henry Hub traded at $2.20-2.23 per mmBtu, up about two cents from Tuesday.
Similarly in south Texas prices climbed two cents to about $2.11-2.13.
In the East, New York city gate prices remained in the mid-$2.40s as forecasters called for a return of warmer temperatures this weekend.
In the Midwest, prices gained about one cent to $2.05-2.06, with Chicago city-gate quoted at $2.21-2.24.
Temperatures in Chicago were expected to reach highs around 80 degrees F through Friday, according to Weather Services Corp.
In west Texas, Permian prices rose by about three cents to the $2.04-2.08 as temperatures in southern California still reached highs in the mid-80s F.
Also supported by cooling demand, southern California prices held steady in the low-to-mid $2.20s. San Juan prices climbed into the low-$2 area for non-constrained gas, traders said.

The outage at El Paso Natural Gas Co's Blanco natural gas plant in the San Juan basin continued, expected to cut about 415 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas on Thursday and 240 mmcfd on Friday and Saturday.
Capacity on the North Mainline for deliveries to Topock and South markets will be cut by 195 mmcfd through Thursday for pipeline replacement.
Separately, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have mostly ranged from 85 to 95 bcf, versus a gain of 87 bcf a year ago.
